focus: 把僵住的會議逼出決定
lead: 上週練的是開場給地圖、把跑掉的討論拉回來。今天練更難的一種主持：房間不是吵起來，而是僵住了 —— 大家都有意見、沒人願意拍板。心法 —— 不要繼續收集意見，把一個提案放上桌，然後宣告「不決定的預設值是什麼」。每個 speaking 段落請先出聲講完再看 model answer。

phrases.en: Let me put a proposal on the table and you can shoot at it.
phrases.gl: 我先丟一個提案，你們來打（僵局時最有效的一招：反對一個具體提案，比憑空產生共識容易十倍）
phrases.ex: We've been circling for twenty minutes. Let me put a proposal on the table and you can shoot at it: we go with software timestamp alignment for the next build.

phrases.en: If we don't decide today, the default is ___ — and I don't think anyone wants that.
phrases.gl: 講出「不決定的後果」（把「不決定」也變成一個選項，大家才會發現它其實最糟）
phrases.ex: If we don't decide today, the default is that we miss the six-week lead time and ship the next build with no hardware sync at all — and I don't think anyone wants that.

phrases.en: What specifically would change your mind?
phrases.gl: 你要看到什麼才會改變想法？（對付「資料不夠、再看看」最鋒利的一句，逼對方把模糊的不安變成具體條件）
phrases.ex: You want two more weeks of logging — what specifically would change your mind? If 40 milliseconds of drift is the threshold, we already have that number.

phrases.en: I'm giving this five more minutes, then I'm going to make a call.
phrases.gl: 公開倒數，並預告你會自己決定（不是威脅，是讓大家知道沉默不會換來延期）
phrases.ex: I'm giving this five more minutes, then I'm going to make a call and you can escalate to David if you disagree.

phrases.en: I'm reading silence as agreement — so speak now.
phrases.gl: 把沉默明確定義成同意（東亞會議最大的陷阱是「沒人反對」不等於「大家同意」，要當場講破）
phrases.ex: I'm reading silence as agreement on the software path — so speak now, because I'm not re-opening this in September.
phrases.fix: 取代 “Everyone OK? … no comment means agree”

phrases.en: We closed this two weeks ago. Has something actually changed?
phrases.gl: 這題兩週前結案了，是有新資訊嗎？（禮貌但堅定地擋掉舊議題重開，把舉證責任丟回去）
phrases.ex: Grace, we closed the mounting position two weeks ago. Has something actually changed, or is this the same concern? If it's new data I'll re-open it.

phrases.en: Let me write that down as the decision while you're all still here.
phrases.gl: 當場把決定打進紀錄，並唸出來（會後才寫，措辭就會被各自解讀）
phrases.ex: Let me write that down as the decision while you're all still here: software alignment for the next build, hardware sync box re-evaluated in November. Vincent, is that what you just agreed to?
phrases.fix: 取代 “I will document this and send out later”

phrases.en: We're done in twenty — I'm giving you the other twenty-five back.
phrases.gl: 提早結束就直接結束，並且明講（準時甚至提早收，是主持人最有效的信用累積）
phrases.ex: That's everything. We're done in twenty — I'm giving you the other twenty-five back. Go get your Friday afternoon.

setup: Setup. You are chairing a forty-five minute architecture review on camera trigger and sync for the next platform build, and this is the third time this decision has been on the agenda. There are two options: a hardware sync box, which costs about eleven hundred dollars per vehicle and has a six-week lead time, or software timestamp alignment, which is free but leaves roughly forty milliseconds of residual drift between the front camera and the GNSS log. Vincent from systems keeps asking for two more weeks of logging before he commits, Grace wants to re-open the camera mounting position that the group already closed two weeks ago, and Alan has said nothing for twenty minutes. David, the program manager, is not on this call — he told you to come back with a decision, not with options.

prompts.q: Twenty minutes in. Everyone has an opinion, nobody has made a proposal, and the same three points have now been made twice each.
prompts.frame: Name the pattern out loud → put one concrete proposal on the table → give the one reason it's the right call → name the default if nobody decides → invite attack, not agreement.
prompts.say: 先出聲講完整段（目標 40 秒）。不要問 “So what do you all think?” —— 僵局裡再問意見只會更僵。
prompts.model: “Okay, let me name what's happening: we've made the same three points twice each, and nobody's actually proposed anything. So let me put a proposal on the table and you can shoot at it. We go with software timestamp alignment for the next build. One reason: forty milliseconds of drift hurts us on cut-in timing, but a six-week lead time on the sync box means we miss the build entirely, and a late perfect solution is worth less to us than an okay one on time. And here's the thing — if we don't decide today, the default isn't that we keep thinking about it. The default is that we blow the lead time and ship with no sync solution at all, which is strictly worse than either option in this room. So don't tell me you agree. Tell me what's wrong with it.”

prompts.q: Vincent: “I really don't think we have enough data to make this call. Can we run another two weeks of logging and come back?”
prompts.frame: Take the request seriously in one clause → ask what specifically would change his mind → convert his answer into a threshold → show whether you already have that number → close the exit or grant it with a hard date.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「拆解『資料不夠』」——不要直接說 no，要把他的模糊不安逼成一個可以檢查的條件。
prompts.model: “That's a fair instinct, Vincent, and I don't want to steamroll you. But let me push on it: what specifically would change your mind? Because if the answer is ‘more data,’ two more weeks gets us more of the same data, not different data. … Okay, so what you actually want to know is whether the drift is stable or whether it grows over a long drive. That's a real question, and it's a narrow one. We already have four long-route logs from June — I can have Alan pull the drift curve on those by Monday, and that answers it without touching the schedule. So here's what I'd like: we make the software call today, contingent on that drift curve. If Alan comes back Monday and the drift is growing past a hundred milliseconds, I'll re-open it myself and go to David for the hardware money. If it's flat, we're done and we don't revisit. Can you live with that?”

prompts.q: Vincent is in. Grace starts back in on the camera mounting position. You have the decision and twenty-five minutes left on the clock.
prompts.frame: Block the re-opened item with a fair test → state the decision plus its condition → write it down live and read it back → name the two owners and dates → end the meeting early, out loud.
prompts.say: 出聲練習「結案並提早散會」——每個 action 要有人名和日期，而且要把提早結束當成一件好事講出來。
prompts.model: “Grace, hold on — we closed the mounting position two weeks ago. Has something actually changed? If you've got new data I'll genuinely re-open it, but if it's the same concern, I want to protect the decision we just made. … Right, then let's leave it closed and I'll send you the June comparison so you can check it yourself. Let me write this down as the decision while you're all still here. Decision: software timestamp alignment for the next platform build. Condition: Alan pulls the drift curve from the four June long-route logs by Monday end of day, and if drift exceeds a hundred milliseconds we re-open and I take the hardware sync box to David for funding. Vincent, is that what you just agreed to? … Good. Two owners: Alan on the drift curve by Monday, me on telling David we have a decision, today. That's everything — we're done in twenty and I'm giving you the other twenty-five back. Thanks, everyone.”

fixes.bad: I want to make decision in this meeting, not only collect opinion.
fixes.good: I want to make a decision in this meeting, not just collect opinions.
fixes.note: Article：decision 是可數單數，前面一定要 a；opinion 這裡是泛指複數，要 opinions。not only 用在對比句需要 but also 收尾，這裡直接用 not just 就好。

fixes.bad: Vincent, can you explain me why the drift is forty milliseconds?
fixes.good: Vincent, can you walk me through why the drift is forty milliseconds?
fixes.note: Preposition：explain 後面不能直接接人，要 explain something to me。母語者在會議裡更常用 walk me through，語氣是「帶我看一遍」，比 explain 少一點質問感。

fixes.bad: Since two weeks we are waiting the vendor to confirm the lead time.
fixes.good: We've been waiting on the vendor to confirm the lead time for two weeks.
fixes.note: Tense：「從兩週前一直到現在」要用現在完成進行式 we've been waiting，不能用現在式；for two weeks 放句尾，since 只能接時間點（since June）不能接時間長度。wait 後面要 on 或 for。

fixes.bad: According to the schedule, we shall finalize the sensor layout in today's meeting.
fixes.good: We need to finalize the sensor layout today.
fixes.note: Register：shall 和 according to the schedule 是公文腔，唸出來像在讀合約。主持人講話要短、要第一人稱、要有時間點 —— 越像人講的話，越有推動力。

fixes.bad: The software option is more safety and also more cheap for us.
fixes.good: The software option is safer, and it's cheaper.
fixes.note: Word form：safety 是名詞，形容詞是 safe，比較級 safer；cheap 是單音節形容詞，比較級直接加 -er 變 cheaper，不加 more。

challenge:
今天在任何一個卡住的討論裡（會議、群組、面對面）做這三步：

1. “Let me put a proposal on the table and you can shoot at it: ___.”

2. “If we don't decide today, the default is ___.”

3. “I'm reading silence as agreement — so speak now.”

錄音作業（60 秒，手機錄）：假設有人說「資料不夠，能不能再等兩週」，錄一段你的回應。

  • 不要直接說 no —— 先問 What specifically would change your mind?
  • 把對方的答案轉成一個可以檢查的門檻（一個數字或一個條件）
  • 提出「今天先決定，但附帶條件」的折衷，並給條件的日期
  • 結尾要回頭確認：Can you live with that?
  • 禁用：explain me、shall、according to the schedule、more cheap
check: 房間僵住的時候，我是繼續收集意見，還是自己丟一個具體提案上桌讓大家打？
有人說「資料不夠」時，我有沒有逼出「到底要看到什麼才願意決定」這個具體門檻？
散會前，我有沒有當著大家的面把決定寫下來、唸出來，並回頭問一句「這是你剛剛同意的嗎」？
